Subject: Fwd: SIG questionnaire and timeline (security review notes)

Vanessa — I reviewed the attached redwood_SIG_responses_v1.xlsx and left comments on the two flagged items. Summary:

1) Key escrow / customer-controlled keys (Q3.4.7)
- Current product supports KMS keys per-customer but we dont have a formal escrow/handover process for EU on-prem hosted backups.
- Proposed interim: allow BYOK with restricted export controls + quarterly attestation that keys are not accessible by Redwood operations.
- Impact: this is a policy/contract exception (security + legal). Product roadmapping needed for any long-term commitment to escrow.

2) Data residency attestations for backups (Q7.1.2)
- We cannot currently provide monthly signed attestations for offsite backups per-customer; we can provide SSAE/SOC reports and region-level controls.
- Proposed interim: quarterly attestation with automated backup-location logs exported on request.

Both items are material enough that they should be escalated to Legal and Sales leadership for approval and for any amendment language. If procurement wants binding timelines (e.g., feature in product roadmap), Product/CTO will need to commit.

I recommend we loop in Markus (Legal) and Vivek (CTO) and ask for a decision by 2026-11-01 so we can meet Aegis procurement window.

-Monica
Sr. Security Engineer, Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference

Vanessa / team,

I reviewed Monicas notes and drafted a narrow amendment that would allow Redwood to provide an interim exception for the two items with the following guardrails:

- Exception is limited in scope and duration (180 days) and specifically enumerates controls (BYOK with quarterly attestation; backlog logs export for backup locations).
- Exception requires customer acknowledgment of the interim nature and automatic review prior to renewal.
- We will include audit rights and additional liability cap for the exceptional scope.

I attached a draft amendment (SIG_exception_amendment_draft.docx). If Sales/Procurement accept the limited exception, Legal can finalize and push to DocuSign.

Note: if Aegis requires a permanent product change (true key escrow or monthly signed attestations), that will need a product roadmap commitment from Vivek and could carry an implementation timeline into H1 2027.

Markus Klein
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
